newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Libya's Gaddafi arrives for visit to Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi arrives for visit to Nigeria.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Friday flew in to an enthusiastic welcome in Kano in northern Nigeria, where he was to lead Moslem prayers and confer with military ruler General Sani Abacha.
Witnesses said Gaddafi arrived from neighbouring Niger and was met at the airport by Abacha, senior officials and local people.
Thousands lined the streets to the airport and Moslem youths carried banners with pictures of Gaddafi and Abacha, two African leaders shunned by the West.
Journalists counted three Libyan planes at Kano airport and were not allowed on the tarmac where he disembarked.
According to an official programme of his visit, Gaddafi was to lead Moslem prayers later in the day at the ultra-modern Kofar Mata mosque in Kano and hold talks with Abacha.
His trip to West Africa is in apparent defiance of a 1992 United Nations embargo on flights from his pariah state.
The ban was imposed for Libya's failure to extradite two agents linked to the bombing of the Pan Am flight over Lockerbie in 1988 and four agents linked to the 1989 bombing of a French airliner.

In Washington, a State Department spokesman said on Thursday the United States was investigating reports that the flight embargo had been broken and if it had been, the matter would be pursued in the U.N. Security Council and sanctions committee. A U.S. official said military action was not being considered.
In Niamey, Gaddafi urged the Moslem world to close ranks and fight colonialism, accusing the United Nations and the Security Council of seeking to destroy Islam.
Gaddafi's last trip abroad was by land to Tunisia in October 1996. He violated the ban when a Libyan-registered plane flew him to Cairo and back to attend an Arab summit in June 1996.
The Libyan news agency JANA on Wednesday said Gaddafi would lead prayers in Niger and Nigeria during a visit as leader of the Islamic Popular Leadership, an organisation he created in 1989.
